function: Deep regression predicts RIS phase shifts and amplitudes, UE powers, blocklength and retransmissions that minimize total power under jamming and URLLC constraints; labels from RBF surrogate optimization (pp. 8-9).
system: Uplink NOMA, K=2 single-antenna UEs, single-antenna BS, jammer, one active reflecting RIS with N=64 elements (N=9 to 900 varied), fc 28 GHz, B 180 kHz (pp. 4, 10).
method: Supervised deep regression network (iota = 100 layers, ReLU, Adam, 10 epochs), one model per blocklength-retransmission class; trained offline on RBF surrogate-optimization labels (pp. 9, 13).
data_channel: Custom MATLAB model: distance path loss (exponent 2) with array-response phase, no fading; scenarios vary jammer power, user distances 5-50 m and azimuths; labels from surrogate optimization (pp. 5, 13).
test_conditions: Same scenario grid for training and test: 60% train, 20% validation, 20% test; model size depends on RIS size N; transfer learning mentioned but not tested (pp. 13-14).
baselines: none: predictions compared only with the surrogate-optimization optimum used as labels, via histograms and WMSE; no classical alternative or learned baseline (pp. 13-14).
metrics: Weighted MSE (10.6 for N=25 to 15.8 for N=196); histograms of predicted versus optimum values; reliability, latency and SJNR of the system (pp. 11-14).
complexity: Offline training takes 1326 s (about 22 minutes) for N=64 on an Intel Core i7 CPU, 32 GB RAM; no inference time, FLOPs or parameter count reported (p. 14).
openness: none: no code or data link; dataset generated from the authors' own MATLAB simulation (p. 13).
q1_support: p. 5: "L is the path gain at the reference distance of 1m"; the channels are custom distance path-loss and array-response vectors with no fading. 3GPP is cited only for the maximum retransmissions (page 10); no 3GPP channel, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 14: "20% of the whole data set is assigned for test data"; the test split is held out from the same scenario grid, each RIS size N has its own model, and transfer learning is only said to be possible, never tested.
q3_support: p. 14: "solver is to compare the distribution of the predicted values" with the surrogate optimum that supplied the training labels. No classical alternative and no earlier learned method is compared on any performance metric.
q4_support: p. 14: "The training process takes 1326 seconds" (about 22 minutes for N=64, on an Intel Core i7 CPU with 32 GB RAM). This is a measured offline training time; no inference time, FLOPs or parameter count is given.
q5_support: p. 13: "To generate a data set" for the DL entity, from the authors' own MATLAB simulation and surrogate optimization (page 10); no link, DOI or repository for code or data, and no public dataset.
notes: Included, area 3: the deep regression (Sec. III-C) outputs RIS phase shifts and amplitudes with UE powers, blocklength and retransmissions for a jammed active-RIS NOMA uplink. The purpose is jamming mitigation (anti-jamming alone is an excluded function) but the learned output is the RIS configuration, so I took area 3; the reviewer should confirm. q4 is 1 only on the measured 1326 s offline training time (p. 14); no inference cost is reported, so confirm. Genetic algorithms appear only as motivation (p. 8) and in one stray sentence (p. 10); no GA result is shown.
